text:
Aisha: sharing the postmortem link for last night's rollout issue: https://redwood.ai/postmortems/2026-03-19-canary-failure 
Aisha: TL;DR: bad config + insufficient blast radius limits, cascade when a model variant returned malformed payloads. Need concrete follow-ups.
Tom: saw it, thanks. I think the highest priority is an automated rollback rule when schema validation fails >5% for 2 minutes.
Riley: +1. also we should cap canary traffic by endpoint, not just by service. right now one noisy route took the whole pool.
Devon: I can own end-to-end on rollout controls. Proposal: implement a new guardrail in the deploy service that enforces per-route canary caps + a hard circuit breaker.
Aisha: thanks Devon — can you add a short plan with ownership and dates to the postmortem follow-ups? want us to ship the emergency guardrails within 2 weeks.
Devon: assigning myself. Plan: 1) telemetry hook + metric (schema_fail_rate_by_route) — due 2026-03-26; 2) per-route canary cap enforcement in deploy service — due 2026-04-02; 3) auto-rollback policy config + tests — due 2026-04-06.
Tom: I'll implement the auto-rollback config. initial idea: rollback when schema_fail_rate_by_route > 0.05 && error_rate > 0.03 for 120s. snippet below for deploy config:
```
rollback_policy:
  triggers:
    - name: schema-validation
      metric: schema_fail_rate_by_route
      threshold: 0.05
      duration: 120s
    - name: error-spike
      metric: http_error_rate
      threshold: 0.03
      duration: 120s
  action: auto_rollback
  limit: per_route
```
Tom: will put a draft PR #3421 today, CCing Riley for review.
Riley: i'll review PR #3421 and add per-route enforcement in PR #3450. also suggest we add a small canary sample set (5 routes max) to avoid one route dominating.
Aisha: good call. add a short regression test that simulates a malformed payload flood against a single route.
Devon: logging playbook items: owner, impact, rollback threshold, test plan. I'll create a checklist in the postmortem doc and in the release board.
deploy-bot: "deploy-bot: canary deployment 2026-03-19T23:14 triggered: model-v2 -> 10% across service (note: route /generate took ~70% of that 10%)"
Riley: we should also add a recurring query in SLO dashboards to surface routes with high variance in request distribution. I'll add that to my tasks.
Tom: estimated dev time: 2 days for rollback logic + 1 day for tests + 1 day for infra review. target PR merge by 2026-03-24.
Aisha: let's sync Friday for a status check. If blockers pop up, escalate to platform oncall.
Devon: noted. I'll update the follow-ups section with owners and deadlines now.
Aisha: thanks everyone. feel free to @me if you need scope cuts. :thumbsup:
